candidate.answerReason: Completing the star with four corner quarter-circles gives a square of side 4. The star has area 16−4π, and the original circle has area 4π, giving the ratio (4−π)/π.

methods.label: Complete a square around the star
methods.explanation:
Each arc is one fourth of the original circle. Completing an arc with its two radii therefore makes a quarter-circle of radius \(2\), with a right angle at its center.

Draw these radii on the outside of the star. They complete a surrounding square, with one quarter-circle at each corner. Each side of the square consists of two radii meeting at a star tip, so its length is \(2+2=4\).

The square has area \(4^2=16\). The four corner quarter-circles have no overlapping interiors and together have the area of one full circle of radius \(2\), namely \(4\pi\). Removing them leaves the star, whose area is
\[
16-4\pi.
\]
The original circle also has area \(4\pi\), so the requested ratio is
\[
\frac{16-4\pi}{4\pi}
=\frac{4-\pi}{\pi}.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
